sources.title: A. R. Rahman (Q108560) -- verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-10-23): English label 'A. R. Rahman', description 'Indian composer and musician', Korean label 'A. R. 라만', citizenship India, no date of death; date of birth is recorded twice (6 January 1966 and 6 January 1967). Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Fukuoka Prize 2016 Grand Prize laureate profile, 'A. R. Rahman' (fukuoka-prize.org, PDF of the laureate page), read in full: composer, songwriter and singer, born 6 January 1967 in Chennai; played keyboard with various orchestras and composers 1987-92; more than 300 advertising and television jingles; the 1992 score for Mani Ratnam's Roja (National Film Award and Tamil Nadu State Film Award for music direction), music director for over 50 films by directors including Mani Ratnam, Shaad Ali, Ashutosh Gowariker and S. Shankar; Bombay Dreams for Andrew Lloyd Webber; Time rating the Roja soundtrack among its all-time top-10 movie soundtracks and the Guardian listing the Bombay soundtrack in its 1000 albums to hear before you die; founder of KM Music label, the KM Music Conservatory and the A. R. Rahman Foundation; two 2009 Academy Awards, a BAFTA, a Golden Globe and two Grammys for Slumdog Millionaire; Padma Shri 2000 and Padma Bhushan 2010; the SuperHeavy band project. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE (with the Berklee page). Prize-body profile, admiring; the 2016 award is a recognition document, not an assessment.

Berklee College of Music, 'A. R. Rahman awarded honorary doctorate' (college.berklee.edu, October 2014), read in full: honorary doctor of music presented 25 October 2014 for professional achievement and contributions to contemporary music; describes him as performer, producer and multi-instrumentalist who began with advertising jingles and drew wide attention with the 1992 Roja score; lists Bombay, Dil Se, Lagaan, Slumdog Millionaire and 127 Hours and collaborations with Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, Andrew Lloyd Webber and the Black Eyed Peas; credits him with founding the KM Music Conservatory in Chennai; praise from Alan Silvestri and Hans Zimmer on his influence. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE (with the Fukuoka Prize page). Institutional honour page, admiring; its remarks on family background, philanthropy and performances for officials were not used.

Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance, 'Honorary President A.R. Rahman' (trinitylaban.ac.uk), read in full: describes him as composer, multi-instrumentalist, educator and producer; works named include Slumdog Millionaire, 127 Hours, a 2012 London Olympics song, Bombay Dreams and a stage version of The Lord of the Rings; the KM Music Conservatory, established in 2008 in Chennai and offering education in all aspects of music and music technology; the Sunshine Orchestra (2008) giving free musical training to disadvantaged children; Honorary Fellowship of Trinity College London (2009); a 2024 partnership agreement between Trinity Laban and the conservatory after years of exchange. Institutional page, admiring; its UN-ambassador, charity-fundraising and family passages were not used.

The News Minute, 'AR Rahman may have been jamming in US night clubs had Mani Ratnam not discovered him' (4 April 2017; excerpt from Kamini Mathai's book 'A. R. Rahman: The Musical Storm'), read in full: the early-1990s sequence in which Mani Ratnam's cousin and her husband, who knew Rahman's jingle work, pitched him to the director; Ratnam visited the young composer's studio and then said nothing for months before offering Thiruda Thiruda and then Roja; another director signed him with an advance; Roja became a national phenomenon and won him the National Award, while Thiruda Thiruda was a box-office failure though its score is still rated among his best; he has kept scoring one director's commercially unsuccessful films, at times unpaid. Biographer's excerpt carried by a news site: outside voices, but a single narrative; the passages about his family circumstances and study plans were not used.

David Benjamin, 'A.R. Rahman Talks Slumdog Millionaire Music', The Playlist, 14 November 2008 (summarising Rahman's New York magazine interview), read in full: Danny Boyle approached Rahman, who was committed to other Indian film work and had to leave another project; Boyle wanted a driving, pulse-heavy, unsentimental score (Rahman quotes his 'no cello' instruction); the score pairs modern Indian sound with 1980s Hindi film soundtrack styles; about two months of planning and about two weeks of completion, compared with around six months for his usual Indian musicals; the track O... Saya made with M.I.A. by exchanging files by email, she recording vocals in England and he finishing the rest in India. Contemporaneous trade-blog summary of a self-interview: the process details are Rahman's own account (self), so used only with corroboration.

Areeba Hashmi, 'AR Rahman secretly made Slumdog Millionaire's Oscar score in 3 weeks', Gulf News, 10 September 2026 (reporting Rahman's YouTube interview with Hasan Minhaj), read in full: Boyle approached him, his agent warned that Boyle might discard a score; he left a prior commitment and kept the project quiet; about three weeks for the score, composed in New York, Mumbai and Chennai and mixed in London; Boyle visited each evening to hear new material and give notes; the Jai Ho dance sequence had been filmed to another song, so he wrote an original track to fit the footage, and Boyle asked for more strings, which Rahman arranged and played back the same day. Retelling of a self-interview (self); the timeline (three weeks) differs from the two-month-plus-two-weeks account of 2008, which is noted rather than reconciled. Not used alone for any row.

Arkadev Ghoshal, 'From Isai Puyal to Oscar-winner and beyond: 30 years of AR Rahman', The South First, 15 August 2022, read in full: career chronology (Roja 1992, Rangeela 1995 and the Hindi breakthrough, the Mani Ratnam films, Lagaan shortlisted for the Oscars, Bombay Dreams with Andrew Lloyd Webber in London and on Broadway, Elizabeth: The Golden Age, the Slumdog Millionaire wins); remarks by collaborators quoted or cited (Asha Bhosle on recording for him with only a flute track, Ram Gopal Varma initially hearing a Carnatic concert in a requested song that later grew on him, Shekhar Kapur's 'slow poison' description of his music, Gulzar, Karan Thapar on his brief interview answers); a song delivered to Varma on cassette within a few days; and a critical section: the 2010 Commonwealth Games theme widely panned as below his usual standard (rearranged days before the event) and its fee criticised, a lukewarm reception for a 2019 Avengers: Endgame song, and a collaboration judged forgettable. Independent journalist's retrospective with collaborator voices and a critical counter-voice. Its passages on religion and his father were not used.

Wikimedia Commons file page 'A.R. Rahman at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival.jpg' (with the Commons API record) -- checked for the portrait: own work of photographer Desmond Herzfelder, taken 6 September 2025 at the Toronto International Film Festival under the WikiPortraits campaign, licence CC BY 4.0. Rights-basis page; no person-specific claim rests on it.

collaboration.rationale: [src_arr_berklee, src_arr_trinity, src_arr_southfirst, src_arr_playlist, src_arr_gulfnews | 1990s-2024 | institution pages + journalist retrospective + two self-interview retellings] Berklee lists work with Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, Andrew Lloyd Webber and the Black Eyed Peas; the South First retrospective reports his Bombay Dreams stage work with Lloyd Webber in London and on Broadway, singer Asha Bhosle recording for him from a bare flute track, and a director's initial doubt about a song that later grew on him; in his own accounts of Slumdog Millionaire (self, 2008 and 2026) he played Boyle early material, took the director's evening notes and, when asked for more strings, delivered an arrangement the same day, and built O... Saya with M.I.A. by exchanging files across two countries; Trinity Laban describes years of exchange with its conservatory before a 2024 partnership. The collaborations are documented by independent institutions and a journalist, while the working detail is largely his own telling, so a documented row at a moderate confidence.

adaptability.rationale: [src_arr_southfirst, src_arr_fukuoka, src_arr_playlist, src_arr_gulfnews | 1992-2019 | journalist retrospective + prize profile + self-interview retellings] The South First retrospective traces a move from Tamil film to a Hindi breakthrough (Rangeela, 1995), to London and Broadway theatre, to Hollywood and British films, and notes he rearranged the 2010 Commonwealth Games theme days before the event after criticism; the Fukuoka profile lists his Tamil, Hindi, English-language and stage credits; for Slumdog Millionaire he composed a new track to fit a dance sequence already filmed to another song (Gulf News, his account) and wrote to a director's brief for a loud, no-cello score (The Playlist, his account). Range across industries and formats is documented by three sources, the reworking episodes rest on his own telling, and the lukewarm reception of some later work shows the move was not always successful, so strong inference at a modest confidence.

creative_originality.rationale: [src_arr_fukuoka, src_arr_playlist, src_arr_southfirst, src_arr_berklee | 1992-2009 | prize profile + press + journalist retrospective + institution page] The Fukuoka profile reports Time rating the Roja soundtrack in its all-time top ten and the Guardian listing the Bombay soundtrack in a thousand-albums list; The Playlist describes the Slumdog Millionaire score as pairing modern Indian sound with 1980s Hindi film styles; the South First retrospective quotes Shekhar Kapur calling his music a 'slow poison' and Ram Gopal Varma first hearing a Carnatic concert in a song that later grew on him, but also records the Commonwealth Games theme as widely panned and a 2019 song as lukewarm; Berklee's praise from Silvestri and Zimmer cites influence on global music. Distinctive, widely recognised work is described by four sources, but the praise is retrospective and institutional and the retrospective itself records uneven results, so strong inference at a modest confidence.

proactive_agency.rationale: [src_arr_fukuoka, src_arr_tnm, src_arr_trinity, src_arr_berklee | 1987-2024 | prize profile + book excerpt + institution pages] Fukuoka records keyboard work with orchestras from 1987, more than 300 jingles, a music label and the founding of the KM Music Conservatory and a foundation; the Trinity Laban page says the conservatory was established in 2008 as the first institution of its kind in India offering education in all aspects of music and music technology, with a Sunshine Orchestra giving free training to disadvantaged children and a 2024 exchange partnership; the News Minute excerpt describes a jingle business built before film work and a composer who kept scoring a director's unsuccessful films. Self-started ventures and institutions are documented, but the descriptions are institutional and admiring and say little about how decisions were made, so strong inference at a modest confidence.

execution_speed.rationale: [src_arr_playlist, src_arr_gulfnews, src_arr_southfirst | 2008-2010 | two self-interview retellings + journalist retrospective] The Playlist (2008) reports about two months of planning and two weeks of completion for the Slumdog Millionaire score against around six months for his usual Indian musicals; Gulf News (2026) reports three weeks in his later retelling, with Boyle's evening visits; the South First retrospective says he delivered a requested song to a director on cassette within a few days and rearranged the Commonwealth Games theme days before the event. The speed claims are mostly his own, differ between tellings, and describe a few episodes rather than a pattern. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): first-pass 62 / 0.50 lowered to 58 / 0.42 because the main support is his own, inconsistent timeline for one project plus two brief anecdotes.

Original 6000 x 4000 pixels (SHA-1 fdf9a65098f678859943ce19d0f2549cf44b2c46); saved as a 960 x 1240 crop from a downscaled 1920 x 1280 rendition of the original, never upscaled. The lead's first-listed lead image (Silverscreen Media, 'Marvel Anthem Launch', CC BY-SA 3.0) was checked and not chosen: it is a press-outlet event photograph whose Commons page cites the outlet's website gallery as source and rests on a licence review, whereas the chosen file is the photographer's own upload.

provenance.notes: PREFLIGHT: QID VERIFIED LIVE: Wikidata wbgetentities (2026-10-23) for Q108560 returned en label 'A. R. Rahman', description 'Indian composer and musician', ko label 'A. R. 라만', citizenship India, no death date, birth recorded twice (1966-01-06 and 1967-01-06), P18 'AR Rahman At The Marvel Anthem Launch.jpg'. BIRTH YEAR: the lead's hint said 1966; the Fukuoka Prize profile gives 6 January 1967 and Wikidata holds both, so 1967 is used (a documented ambiguity, not a scored fact). SLUG/QID CHECK: no production or candidate file for slug a-r-rahman or QID Q108560 in the roster53 worktree (grep over data-pipeline, src/data, src/core). REGION: south_asia, nationalityCodes IN. VOCABULARY: occupations composer and musician, fields music and film, impact domains artistic and cultural, tags innovator and prolific, archetype creative_creator are existing ids with labels. ZERO POLITICS: nothing political scored or carded (UN-ambassador and charity passages in sources excluded). LIVING SUBJECT: only documented public professional behaviour scored. EXCLUDED deliberately: religion and conversion, family, childhood circumstances and bereavement, health and any mental-state remark, finances, the resurfaced 2026 'Jai Ho' authorship claims and any other allegation or rumour, plagiarism talk, interview-personality remarks, memoir and fan-site translations (Rahmaniac reproductions are rights-reserved fan material and were not cited). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Fukuoka Prize 2016 laureate profile (https://fukuoka-prize.org/files/download/en/LaureatesI18n/laureate_blocks/d7051551-0c01-4e75-96c9-5c65ce5c70c8/value01/value02; read in full) and Berklee honorary-doctorate page (https://college.berklee.edu/news/ar-rahman-awarded-honorary-doctorate; read in full). READ (7 cited sources plus the Commons page): Fukuoka, Berklee, Trinity Laban, The News Minute book excerpt, The Playlist, Gulf News, The South First. Opened but not usable: Britannica (HTTP 403), NPR transcript (timeout), World Music Central (HTTP 409), Time 100 entry (wrong page returned). Not opened: Guardian, NYT and Hindu originals (blocked to the fetch tool), the Vikatan interview translation on a fan site, the Krishna Trilok book. PERSPECTIVES: prize body and two conservatories (honour pages), a biographer's excerpt carried by a news site, a journalist's 30-year retrospective with collaborator voices (Bhosle, Varma, Kapur, Gulzar) and critical remarks, and two self-interviews retold by trade press (self; used only with corroboration). COUNTER-VOICE: The South First on the panned Commonwealth Games theme, the lukewarm Endgame song and a forgettable collaboration. LIMITATIONS: independent behavioural evidence is thin; no detailed account by a collaborator such as Boyle or Ratnam was readable, so no row is above 68 or 0.56 and no row on risk, perfectionism, studio routine or deep focus is claimed. PORTRAIT: Commons page and API read; creator and own-work upload by Desmond Herzfelder (6 Sep 2025, CC BY 4.0, original 6000x4000); the Silverscreen Media 'Marvel Anthem Launch' lead image (CC BY-SA 3.0, Dani Charles, 800x1200) was checked and passed over because it is an outlet's event photograph sourced from the outlet's gallery with only a licence-review tag. No institutional conflicting notice applies. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): the highest-risk rows reviewed were execution speed (self-reported, inconsistent timeline; lowered 62/0.50 to 58/0.42), creative originality (retrospective praise, but already modest at 64/0.52 and the sources include critical results; left unchanged) and collaboration (partly self-told, but corroborated by Berklee, Trinity Laban and the South First retrospective; left unchanged). No broad scoring problem flagged.
